end.summary:
- Practised writing repeated multiplication as exponential form and identifying base and exponent; easy questions were right, but a why/new-situation check is still needed.
- Practised evaluating powers, including negative bases; some answers were right, but the method was not steady yet.
- Initially swapped base and exponent, then corrected this using repeated multiplication; 2⁵ and 5² were compared correctly.
- Initially read 3⁴ as repeated addition, then used multiplication and reached 81.
- Practised sign patterns for (−2)⁴ and (−2)³; next time, check more examples independently.
end.parentNote: Kavya practised connecting repeated multiplication to exponential notation and used paired negative factors to work on powers with negative bases. The base/exponent mix-up and the repeated-addition reading of 3⁴ were corrected later in the lesson; Kavya also noticed that swapping base and exponent changes the answer. At home, ask them to expand and evaluate a few examples such as 2³, 3², (−3)², and (−3)³, explaining why each sign is positive or negative.
